tieu_de: Pluto transit through the 4th house: digging up the foundations
mo: Will I have to move house during Pluto in the 4th?
Why are childhood memories coming back now?
How can I handle conflict with parents or siblings?

Your home and your family history sit at the bottom of the chart, in the 4th house. When Pluto passes through, it goes all the way down. People often move, renovate or take on care of a parent. Underneath those visible changes, something older gets stirred: the emotional ground you were raised on.
It can be a heavy period. It is also one of the best chances you will have to repair what was laid down in childhood and build a private life that truly shelters you.

doan: The 4th house represents home, family, roots, parents and the inner sense of safety you carry around. Pluto transforms what it touches from the bottom up. Here that means your living situation and your emotional foundation both come up for renewal.

The work is double. On the outside, there is the practical side of houses, walls, moves and family logistics. On the inside, there is the older story of how you were cared for and what you learned about belonging.
Planet Pluto Rules Scorpio Transformation, rebirth, power

A move is common, sometimes planned and sometimes forced by circumstances. So is a major renovation, the kind where walls come down and you live in dust for months. Some people inherit a family property or have to clear out a parent's house.

Family members may need more of your attention. A parent's needs change. Siblings disagree about who does what. Old family roles, the responsible one, the peacemaker, the one who left, reassert themselves and ask to be looked at.
Emotionally, memories from childhood may come back unexpectedly: a smell, a song, a dream. You may notice patterns in your reactions that clearly started long ago.

This transit is especially well suited to therapy, counselling or any serious work on early experiences. Things that were too buried to reach before become accessible. Many people describe feeling more at home in themselves once this work is done.

On a practical level, you have the chance to create a living space that reflects who you are now rather than who you were expected to be. That can mean a new home, a rebuilt one, or simply a different way of living in the one you have.

Family power dynamics can become intense. Arguments about property, inheritance or care can reopen old wounds. There may be pressure to take on more responsibility than is fair, or a pull to cut off family entirely rather than deal with what is painful.

Home can also feel less safe for a while during the rebuilding, whether physically or emotionally. Practical matters need care too: check the condition of your house and review your property insurance so an avoidable problem does not become a bigger one.

Pluto takes 12 to 30 years to cross a sign, and a house transit is often of similar length. Your house system and birth latitude can make the 4th house larger or smaller, so your own chapter may run shorter or longer than average. Pluto crossing the IC, the cusp of the 4th house, often marks the moment the transit is felt most keenly, and retrograde motion can bring several passes over that point.
If you have ever considered therapy, this is the time to start. Choose someone experienced with family history and give it more than a few sessions.
Take care of the building. Arrange an inspection, fix what has been ignored, and read your insurance policy properly. Small practical steps give the emotional work a stable base.
In family matters, say clearly what you can and cannot take on. Guilt is a poor guide to fair responsibility.
Stop carrying family secrets alone if they are hurting you. Start building rituals at home that feel like your own, even simple ones like how you spend a Sunday morning.

A move is common but not guaranteed. Some people renovate instead, and some change the household by someone moving in or out. The underlying theme is renewing your base, which can happen in several ways.

The 4th house holds your earliest emotional foundations. Pluto brings buried material to the surface so it can be dealt with. It is uncomfortable, but it is also the reason this transit is such a good time for healing work.

Keep the focus on what is happening now rather than reopening every past grievance at once. Set clear limits, get outside help if needed, and remember that the goal is a healthier family pattern, not winning.
